title: MMSBUILD delivery board
note: Modules are the PRD's phases, tasks are its requirements, subtasks are its acceptance criteria. Ids match the PRD exactly, so an acceptance run maps to this board line for line. `status` is ours — what is built. `verified` belongs to the acceptance run and is never set by us.

verified.pending: Not yet run by the other party

modules.title: Phase 0 — Close the surface
modules.summary: Every requirement after this one assumes an authenticated admin.

tasks.title: Admin authentication
tasks.note: Built 2026-09-17: every admin route on the control plane and every console page requires a signed-in administrator — scrypt password, a signed 12-hour session scoped to the console, per-email lockout after repeated failures. One check sits ahead of every route, and a self-test fails if an admin route is ever left outside it. The connector keeps site creation only, on its own token. The board is no longer served on the public address. Live since 2026-09-17: on the public address every admin route answers 401 without a session, the console redirects to sign-in, and the public board path is gone.

subtasks.text: Unauthenticated admin request refused; the console requires sign-in

tasks.title: The admin surface reveals no secret it does not have to
tasks.note: Built 2026-09-17: machine keys are stored as a hash only, the read-back route is gone, and stored copies are wiped at startup. The project listing carries no invite link, no AI gateway token and no secret-bearing field; a new invite link is shown once, when issued. Links already shared keep working until used or replaced. Live since 2026-09-17: a signed-in project listing carries no invite link, token or secret-bearing field, and a key read-back answers 404.

subtasks.text: A minted machine key cannot be read back in plaintext
A project listing leaks no usable invite link or capacity token

modules.title: Phase 1 — The levels
modules.summary: Operator and Business above Project, with roles that hold when the interface is bypassed.

tasks.title: Operator and Business levels above Project
tasks.note: Built 2026-09-17: Operators own Businesses, Businesses own projects, and a Business with no Operator sits directly under the platform. Every stored record carries its Operator and Business, stamped by the database, so moving a project or a Business re-addresses everything under it. Console accounts are scoped to the platform, one Operator or one Business; every read and change is limited to that scope, and a project outside it answers "not found". The chain is listed in the console's Organisation page and by the organisation API. The existing projects each became a Business of their own; the staging copy shares its site's. Project processes now hold only their own signing key and no control-plane credentials, so a project cannot reach another Business through its own server either. Builder smoke test 2026-09-17: an Operator and a Business under it were created in the console. The console was then redesigned to match the MMS-CMS — the shared MMS header, pages in setup order (Organisation → Projects → People → Access), dialogs for every create and change, confirmations for destructive actions, and themed dropdowns. Builder check 2026-09-18: the redesigned console was confirmed working. Two faults found in that check are fixed — a dropdown inside a dialog drew its options behind the dialog, so they were invisible, and the console was being served in development mode, which made every page fetch its source file by file. The console now runs from its build and each page asks the control plane for everything it needs at once: pages that took 1–2 seconds now answer in 15–30 ms.

subtasks.text: The Operator → Business → Project chain is queryable; each level resolves its children
Cross-Business read and write denied at the server; no foreign data in any listing

tasks.title: Roles, and more than one person per project
tasks.note: Built 2026-09-17: a project has any number of people, each with one of the CMS's own four roles — Owner, Publisher (the CMS admin role), Author (the CMS client role: edits content, cannot publish) and Viewer. People are invited, re-roled and removed from the console's People page. The CMS enforces the role on every request, so a denial holds for a direct call as well as in the interface. A role change or removal reaches the CMS at once, including for a session that is already open. Live since the 2026-09-17 restart.

subtasks.text: Publisher-role action allowed; the same action denied to an author role
The denial holds when the interface is bypassed

tasks.title: Inviting a second person must not overwrite the first
tasks.note: Built 2026-09-17: an invite adds an account. Re-inviting someone who already has access is refused instead of locking them out; re-inviting someone still invited only replaces their link. When one email belongs to several projects, sign-in asks which project rather than picking one. Live since the 2026-09-17 restart.

subtasks.text: A second invite adds an account rather than replacing the first

tasks.title: A portal sign-in arrives with its own role, not as the owner
tasks.note: Built 2026-09-17: the hub's signed hand-off names the person and their role; the CMS signs them in as their own account with that role, and the design studio records who is working. Step-up is never pre-satisfied: it asks for the person's hub password, checked by the control plane, and an unreachable check fails. Sessions that the old hand-off opened with step-up already satisfied are ended at upgrade. The design studio's Share to CMS now brings the person into the CMS as themselves. Only the agent gateway and the studio's own server-side staging use a machine sign-in, which the hub never issues. Live since the 2026-09-17 daemon rebuild and restart.

subtasks.text: An author role is denied an owner-only action inside the CMS
Step-up is demanded, not pre-satisfied

modules.title: Phase 4 — Governance, with proof
modules.summary: NEW-4 first: nothing in the approver work functions until both ends agree.

tasks.title: The issuing side resolves per-property approvers too
tasks.note: Built 2026-09-16 (commit c865d10): the relay resolves the approver per property on the same rule the Connector applies — property key alone, no fallback for a property whose key is unusable, malformed configuration keeps the relay shut. Reaches the live relay only when the relay account holder redeploys it.

subtasks.text: A property-specific approval is issued and then accepted by the checking side

tasks.title: Per-property approver: registration, delegation, rotation
tasks.note: Both ends now resolve a per-property approver. Registration, delegation up Project → Business → Operator, and rotation/revocation as first-class operations are not built.

tasks.title: Import and publish each gated, bound, and gated separately
tasks.note: The gate covers eight actions, binds the artefact, expires, is single-use and spends before acting. Outstanding: a property exempted from the gate must not be able to stay exempt in production.

Approval bound to a different artefact: refused
Expired approval: refused
A spent approval presented again: refused

tasks.title: Fail-closed everywhere
tasks.note: The approval policy fails closed. The importability check passes the share through when it crashes, and the pre-flight does not block (R11).

subtasks.text: A crashed importability check blocks, distinguishably from a success
Missing or unreadable policy: every gated action refuses
A check that cannot run yields failure, never a zero-findings pass

tasks.title: The proof chain: receipt, live verification, known-good, immutability
tasks.note: None of receipt, live verification, known-good retention or rollback exists on the platform publish path. Adopt the studio deploy path's deploy record and reachability verifier. The current publish wipes the previous generation first, so retention must come before AC-B9.3 is possible. The build revision exists on responses and in the activity log but is not yet written into a durable deploy record.

subtasks.text: A receipt per publish with every named field present
Verification fetches the site; a missing route serving a fallback is caught as FAIL
A known-good bundle is retained and reconstructs the prior state
Editing or deleting a past receipt is denied

tasks.title: The two ends do not trust each other
tasks.note: Two implementations sharing no code, pinned by shared test vectors. The vectors must grow to cover per-property resolution.

subtasks.text: Verification succeeds with the issuing side offline, using unshared code
A tampered approval fails on the acting side; both sides pass the shared suite
